scope: Xeno Entry Fabric causal event identity for HCU/XCU routing and downstream inference receipts

current_implementation_scope.law: Current Python-local deterministic hashes MUST NOT be represented as proof of heterogeneous Entry-Fabric hash identity. Existing receipts keep their original schema/identity and are never silently reinterpreted under a later canonicalizer.

required_input_constraints: duplicate object property names rejected at raw ingress before ordinary Mapping construction can erase them
all strings are valid Unicode and lone surrogates fail closed
string contents are preserved as-is with no Unicode normalization performed by the canonicalization layer
JSON numbers are finite and representable as IEEE-754 binary64; NaN and Infinity fail closed
higher-precision numeric application values are represented by an explicitly typed string/integer contract rather than silently rounded
required_serialization: JSON primitive serialization follows the RFC 8785 ECMAScript-compatible rules
object properties sort recursively by raw property-name UTF-16 code units
array element order is preserved while objects inside arrays are recursively canonicalized

required_discriminators_before_cross_lan: official RFC 8785 UTF-16 property ordering vector
same admitted typed event canonicalized independently by at least two implementations/languages yields byte-identical canonical output and identical event digest
same event with reordered JSON properties yields identical canonical bytes/digest
duplicate-property raw JSON is rejected before event identity is minted
NaN Infinity lone-surrogate and untyped-extension cases fail closed
numeric edge cases including negative zero exponent formatting and IEEE-754 rounding match the admitted canonicalization contract
causal event digest remains stable across engine resolution while route digest changes when exact engine artifact identity changes
downstream inference receipt with wrong or missing canonicalization version fails closed
note: This contract advances the Xeno Entry Fabric/XPU/XCU identity seam without adding a second state, routing, or effect authority. RFC 8785 is a candidate interoperability mechanism; source documentation alone does not establish conformance.
